assessments.assessment: The single common coset-Helly lemma proves both implications and handles repeated types and empty intersections. Every replaced proof invokes it under flag transitivity. The residue-generation lemma retains the Borel and is used under residual connectedness, including empty support.

The complete normal-form/tree transfer proofs remain present. The fixed coherent amalgamation map, firmness for Boolean parabolics and the active/universal-type reduction are unchanged. The nonfirm S4 obstruction retains all six indexed groups and the literal output formulas. No unrestricted HNN assertion is inferred.

The statement now explicitly imports faithful regular inputs and the indexed action from the regular orbit corollary. Its full proof uses maximal-parabolic images and their intersections, then divides by the action kernel. It does not substitute generated-support images for intersections or assert a faithful quotient group. This clarification preserves all declared applications.

All inverse presentation maps, the separate cyclic coset-Helly argument and the retained Artin interfaces remain written. The newly stated Shephard presentation agrees with the source convention: odd finite pair labels require equal vertex orders. The full-space representation separates generators, without asserting group faithfulness or general Shephard intersection properties.

The complete uniform argument for s>=5 and the complete finite premise for s=2,3,4 remain separate. The literal quotient/twist proof treats all s>=1 and keeps the input failure at s=1 distinct from output regularity. The classical faithful affine realization remains an explicit retained input.

All 81 dispositions and question qualifications are identical to the accepted precursor contract. New introductory application paragraphs invoke the complete common results with matching hypotheses. The original source constructions and results remain attributed to Piedade and Tranchida.

All three programs are unchanged and freshly replayed; every ordered code token occurs in the complete four-page appendix. Only the affine small-parameter program is a required finite premise. Existing partial Lean components retain their declared limits; no new formalization is claimed.

The new common paper contains the complete previous orbit, quotient, orbital-presentation and signed-module arguments. This review does not silently update or admit revised N006/N007 applications: their citation migration and full cost boundary remain a separate obligation.
